title: DJI Mavic 4 Pro live streaming: RC 2 and RC Pro 2 guide (2026)
description: Stream your DJI Mavic 4 Pro with RC 2 or RC Pro 2 to a phone or computer. Check DJI Fly RTMP, microphone differences, 720p limits and platform setup.
h1: How to live stream a DJI Mavic 4 Pro
lead: Your DJI Mavic 4 Pro can send DJI Fly’s RTMP picture to Stream My Drone on a separate phone or Stream My Drone on a computer. The useful starting point is your controller: RC 2 and RC Pro 2 both have screens, but their microphone hardware differs. Follow the route below to receive the picture, choose destinations and check what viewers actually see.
summary: Use RC 2 or RC Pro 2; DJI’s current Mavic 4 Pro setup does not list an RC-N controller.
A separate phone running Stream My Drone gives you a computer-free receiving and forwarding setup.
DJI Fly’s RTMP broadcast is a separate output from the high-resolution recording on the aircraft.
Put the receiving app’s local address in DJI Fly and the platform credentials in the receiving app.
Check the actual RTMP menu and microphone prompt before takeoff, then confirm the platform’s viewer page.

sections.h2: Which Mavic 4 Pro controller can send the feed?

blocks.p: DJI’s aircraft linking guide lists DJI RC 2 and DJI RC Pro 2 for Mavic 4 Pro. Both run DJI Fly on their built-in screen. Do not reuse an RC-N1, RC-N2 or RC-N3 workflow from another aircraft: those are not the controller choices documented for this model.

blocks.note: DJI RC Pro 2 is different from DJI RC Pro. Its official FAQ confirms a built-in microphone. RC 2 users should prepare an external microphone; follow the prompt on the actual DJI Fly version before starting a broadcast.

sections.h2: Check the RTMP menu before planning the broadcast

blocks.p: Update the aircraft, controller and DJI Fly, link the aircraft and enter its camera view. Open GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP. Menu names can differ by version and language. If your firmware does not expose RTMP, the receiving app cannot add it.

blocks.note: DJI’s current livestream operation guide limits both RC 2 and RC Pro 2 RTMP output to 720p. It also requires a connected microphone on RC 2 from DJI Fly v1.16.0. Verify the available output settings on your controller; a 1080p screen or higher aircraft recording setting does not override this limit.

sections.h2: Mavic 4 Pro without a computer: receive on a phone

steps.t: Install Stream My Drone on a separate phone
steps.d: Download it from Google Play or the App Store. Keep DJI Fly open on your RC 2 or RC Pro 2; the phone will receive and forward its video.

steps.t: Put the controller and receiver on the same network
steps.d: Use a Wi-Fi network with internet access. In the field, an Android receiving phone can also host the hotspot. Open Stream My Drone after choosing the network and allow local network access on iPhone when requested. Check the displayed address again if you change networks.

steps.t: Enter the receiver address in DJI Fly
steps.d: Copy the full local RTMP address shown by Stream My Drone. In DJI Fly, open GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP. Follow the labels in your version: a screen asking for separate address and key fields is different from one asking for a full RTMP URL. Do not add your YouTube or Instagram key to the local receiver address. See the DJI Fly RTMP guide for the menu walkthrough.

steps.t: Start the local feed and check sound
steps.d: Start livestreaming in DJI Fly, then verify a moving picture appears in Stream My Drone. Check the microphone selected on the controller and listen at the platform during your ground test. A picture without usable sound is easier to diagnose before takeoff.

Connect a platform account where that option is available, or enter its current server URL and stream key in Stream My Drone. Start forwarding and open the platform dashboard. Complete any separate Go Live step, then confirm the actual viewer page works.

blocks.note: The receiving phone is a separate device from the controller. Mobile forwarding preserves the incoming video; preview cropping or a blurred background does not create a new vertical broadcast. On iPhone, keep the app open during setup; continued background reception depends on Picture in Picture.

sections.h2: Mavic 4 Pro on Mac or Windows: desktop production

blocks.p: Keep DJI Fly running on your RC 2 or RC Pro 2. Install Stream My Drone on your Mac or Windows PC. The computer receives the DJI Fly RTMP feed over your local network; this setup does not use HDMI capture or a USB webcam connection from the controller.

steps.t: Copy the computer’s local RTMP address
steps.d: Connect the computer and the device running DJI Fly to the same network. In Stream My Drone, copy the address under Connect your drone. rtmp://192.168.1.20:1935/drone is only an example: use the address displayed by your app.

steps.t: Send the feed and verify reception
steps.d: Enter that local address in DJI Fly and start streaming. If the firewall asks, allow the app to receive connections on your private network. Check the moving preview before configuring a platform.

steps.t: Choose your output and start a destination
steps.d: Choose landscape or a desktop vertical layout, then add the platform’s server URL and key. Start the output, confirm the platform receives it and complete its publishing step. For several destinations, check the combined upload requirement before enabling them together.

blocks.p: Account eligibility comes from the platform. Neither app grants a stream key or bypasses access requirements. For a computer workflow in a compatible studio app, Stream My Drone also provides a virtual camera. A local preview proves reception; a working viewer page confirms publication.

sections.h2: Recording quality, portrait shooting and your broadcast

blocks.p: Keep three pictures separate: the file recorded on the aircraft, the controller’s live view and the RTMP video arriving at the receiver. Evaluate the stream by its received dimensions and bitrate. A larger desktop output cannot recreate details absent from the incoming image.

Mavic 4 Pro can shoot vertically, and DJI documents the controls in its portrait-mode guide. Test what the RTMP receiver actually gets after changing orientation. A vertical recording setting, a rotated controller screen and a 9:16 platform broadcast are not interchangeable checks.

list: Frame deliberately. Check the outgoing picture at the platform. On mobile, the preview layout does not re-encode it; on desktop, choose the crop or whole-picture output you intend to publish.
Budget per destination. A continuous 5 Mbps output uses about 2.25 GB per hour before overhead. Two such outputs need about 10 Mbps combined upload and 4.5 GB per hour.
Test on the ground. Check movement, sound and the real viewer page. Keep the receiving phone close to the hotspot and monitor its power and temperature during longer broadcasts.

sections.h2: Troubleshooting the Mavic 4 Pro live feed

list: No RTMP option: confirm the controller model and software version in DJI Fly. RC 2 and the older DJI RC have different features; changing the receiver does not change the controller’s capabilities.

DJI Fly asks for a microphone: with RC 2, connect a supported microphone and recheck its input. With RC Pro 2, check the selected input and microphone permissions instead of assuming RC 2 instructions apply.
Connection failed: use the receiver’s current local IP address. Guest Wi-Fi isolation, a firewall or switching hotspots can break the local connection. localhost refers to the controller itself.
Preview works but the audience sees nothing: check forwarding, the destination credentials and any remaining platform Go Live step.
iPhone reception stops: return to Stream My Drone and check Picture in Picture. iOS can suspend reception when the app is in the background without it.

blocks.p: Checked on October 25, 2026: DJI aircraft linking guide for controller choices; DJI RC Pro 2 FAQ for microphone hardware; DJI Fly livestream operation guide for RTMP limitations; and DJI portrait mode for vertical shooting controls. Firmware and menu availability can change; verify your own combination.
For the previous generation, read the Mavic 3, Classic and Pro streaming guide. To send the same feed to several services, continue with multistreaming a DJI drone.

faq.q: Can I live stream Mavic 4 Pro without a computer?
faq.a: Yes, use DJI Fly on RC 2 or RC Pro 2 and receive its RTMP feed in Stream My Drone on a separate phone on the same local network. Configure destinations in the phone app and confirm publication on each platform.

faq.q: Can I use an RC-N3 phone setup with Mavic 4 Pro?
faq.a: DJI’s current linking guide lists RC 2 and RC Pro 2 for this aircraft. This guide uses those supported screen controllers rather than assuming RC-N compatibility from another model.

faq.q: Do both controllers need an external microphone?
faq.a: RC Pro 2 has a built-in microphone. For RC 2, DJI documents a connected-microphone requirement from Fly v1.16.0. Test audio and follow the prompt shown by your controller before flight.

faq.q: Does a 6K recording mean a 6K livestream?
faq.a: No. The file recorded by the camera is separate from the DJI Fly RTMP output. Check the actual input in the receiving app and the stream seen by the platform.

faq.q: Where do my YouTube or Instagram credentials go?
faq.a: In the destination settings of Stream My Drone or Stream My Drone. DJI Fly receives the local RTMP address displayed by that app.

faq.q: Does rotating the controller screen guarantee a vertical broadcast?
faq.a: Check the image arriving in the receiver and the platform’s viewer page. The controller screen, camera recording orientation and outgoing video format are separate. Desktop Stream My Drone can convert output to a vertical layout.
